## Summary

A future topic for this project is **non-compliance patterns** — recurring signals in how
companies meet (or miss) their filing obligations, such as repeatedly late accounts, missing or
unresolved PSC information, and dormancy used to minimise disclosure. These are distinct from the
current per-company [indicator flags](methodology.qmd): the interest is in *patterns over time
and across companies*, not a single company's current state. This page exists to mark the topic;
the analysis is not written.

## Details

Candidate directions, recorded so the scope is visible — **none analysed yet**:

- **Repeatedly late filings.** Reconstructing statutory deadlines (first-accounts rules, deadline
  changes over time, COVID extensions) to identify repeat late filers, rather than counting raw
  filing history. This is the `REPEAT_LATE_FILER` idea already scoped in the project plan as a
  later phase.
- **Missing or unresolved PSC information.** Statement patterns such as "PSC exists but not
  identified" or "steps to find PSC not yet completed" over time — building on the
  [PSC work](../datasets/psc.qmd).
- **Dormancy.** How dormant status is used, and transitions in and out of it.

Each of these is a recorded-fact pattern, not a judgement of wrongdoing, and any future work here
would carry the same guardrails as the rest of the project: traceable to named register fields,
no composite score, no named company results, and the limitations set out on the
[limitations page](limitations.qmd). Until then, there is nothing to read here.
